To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the analytic process of producing I-poems is a useful tool for qualitative longitudinal research because it enables the researcher to identify the voices of the research participant and their social world, as well as the voices of the analyst; (2) the process of producing Ipoems enables the researcher to shift analytic ontology, and to identify the voices in the data that are not heard in thematic analysis, such as the researcher’s voice; (3) Ipoems can be used as a tool
I-poems are a useful analytic tool for exploring change and continuity in the sense of self over the life course.

(i) I-poems provide a different analytic angle from which to view the data than thematic analysis, (ii) I-poems are particularly useful for identifying change over time, and (iii) I-poems can be used as a way of identifying the relationship between the researcher and the interviewee.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the way that different analytic methods construct different modes of being, or analytic ontologies, and the implications this has for the way we understand the interviewee, and the social world.
the ontological implications of analytic choices and how they shape the researcher’s relationship to their data and the people they study.
the ontological and methodological implications of the different analytic positions that qualitative researchers take up.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
I-poems are not the best way to analyse qualitative longitudinal data.
I-poems provide an alternative analytic mode of being that is more relational, more dialogic, and more open to the subjectivity of the research participant.
I-poems are a useful analytic tool for exploring continuity and change in the sense of self over the life course.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thematic analysis provided a ‘view from nowhere’ and the I-poems provided an ‘I’-view from somewhere.
the analytic mode of being provided by I-poems is a useful complement to thematic analysis.
the I-poems provide a more nuanced and detailed account of change and continuity, and a more embodied account of the young person’s sense-making, than the thematic analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
analytic methods can be seen as ontological tools, which can be used to shift our analytic gaze and to reconfigure the relationship between the researcher and the research object.
analytic methods have ontological implications, in the sense that they construct different sorts of relationships between the analyst and the data.
the analytic mode of being that is implicit in a given analytic method can be made explicit, and that this can be useful for researchers and readers alike.
